plan.title: Hampstead: private ambitions and public provision — proposed exterior loop
plan.selectionReason:
Propose this four-stop order for pedestrian routing, followed by independent Scout review; this is not route acceptance. All four existing researched places now have empty essentialUnknowns arrays. In particular, c06 explicitly adopts the reservoir-site exterior anchor, without requiring dome visibility, observatory entry or an observing session. The previous three-stop eligibility assessment is superseded by the supplied revised research.

Station endpoint: use the exterior pavement vertex at 51.5566258,-0.1783709, where outdoor footway 570239725 from named Hampstead entrance A joins pavement way 570239729. The retained read_station_map identifies entrance A, node 5482470204, at 51.5566418,-0.1783414 and station building 103110118; the subsequent successful read_map supplies the adjoining outdoor geometry. This is neither the entrance threshold nor a building centre. Underground station/platform nodes, indoor passages, customer-only lifts and indoor steps were excluded by their tags. Sources: Overpass query hashes 913a08c08aac042968c584d96a67f720d70ffc9152cc4f141c05729daef3381b and 9503952a57de9f328bed50d263355ec0ddc16f99e1dd8583b152e6356f92fb30, retrieved October 7, 2026; © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. The retained 2021 RailScot image supports the exterior setting, not present clearance. This is a map-supported proposed public pavement endpoint, not a surveyed safe gathering area; keep the entrance and passing pedestrians unobstructed.

Outline and visitor positions: (1) Fenton House, c05, 51.55889,-0.17941 on Hampstead Grove pavement: speculative development and domestic wealth, supported by the National Trust. No garden access or gate-cipher recognition required. (2) Admiral's House, c07, 51.55951,-0.18017 on the public footway south of Admiral's Walk: distinguish visible architectural ambition, North's documented rank and accumulated naming stories. Retain the cannon account as something he is said to have done, not witnessed fact. (3) Reservoir/observatory site, c06, 51.5608051,-0.1794126 on public footway 29155571: neighbourhood science and the infrastructure beneath it, attributed to the Society's history. Look towards the site boundary, without promising a dome view. (4) New End, c08, 51.55878,-0.177607 on the Elm Row–New End public footway: contrast private households with changing institutional provision for poverty and sickness. Attribute chronology to Historic England; do not harmonise conflicting dates or identify every visible frontage element as the original workhouse. No Rotunda view or private-estate entry required. These are retained visitor positions, distinct from landmark and camera coordinates; their precision is not survey accuracy.

All five legs are included in the routing proposal: station to c05; c05 to c07; c07 to c06; c06 to c08; c08 back to the identical station pavement endpoint. Test the outward Holly Hill/Hampstead Grove approach and the longer reservoir-to-New End connection as the two principal walking-chapter opportunities; prefer simple public connections, leaving quiet intervals and silence at crossings. Intermediate stops need only short links. These are corridor preferences, not established turn-by-turn directions. The station map records marked crossings, including way 1046350857 towards Holly Hill; the router must connect the appropriate approaches rather than draw straight lines across roads. For the northern-to-eastern connection, resolve the actual Heath Street crossing and public approach to Elm Row/New End. Exclude customer-only grounds, private Upper Hampstead Walk, indoor station paths and shortcuts through residential entrances.

Timing proposal: target 2–3 km only where useful public geometry supports it; accept a shorter compact loop rather than add padding or new candidates. Reserve 480 seconds for looking, crossings and practical pauses, plus approximately 600 seconds stationary narration within the requested 8–12-minute range. At the planning assumption of 1.2 metres per second, 2–3 km would require about 1,667–2,500 seconds walking, giving approximately 2,747–3,580 seconds before any additional hill-related slowing. Thus 3 km has little spare margin: prefer the shorter result if gradients, steps or crossings demand it. No distance or hour-fit is yet measured. Count walking narration within walking time once; any additional stationary listening adds time. Include the return leg, actual rendered narration and hill-adjusted walking before judging the 3,600-second limit.

Scoped unresolved questions for router and Scout: Are all five legs connected by permitted daytime pedestrian routes? What are their measured distances, ascent, steps and crossing delays? Do the four standing positions and station pavement leave adequate clearance, with the stated general exterior views? Are there current closures or restrictions? Maps alone do not settle these questions. Request geometry next, then independent practical review; revise within the same endpoints and duration if necessary, without silently relaxing either. No further history research or candidate expansion is proposed.
